note: Known molten-salt Si work for PV; wafer cost is a small DRAM cost share and 5-6N films are marginal for low-leakage cells.
Dealloyed sponge plate is lab-easy; per-cell top electrode in 20 nm pores and Cu diffusion into dielectric are doubts.
Twist on IBM electrical breakdown; small-gap CNT channels leak too much for DRAM retention.
Salt sacrificial substrates known for lift-off; Na migration and 40 ppm/K CTE mismatch are severe; substrate is not the cost driver.
Novel placement, but memory in the TIM path hurts cooling and a hot setpoint raises leakage.
Vertical VLS wires need an epitaxial seed; printed Sn dots cannot reach DRAM pitch or alignment on oxide foil.
Mica vdW epitaxy is known; cleave-renewal is a twist, but the 600 C ceiling and small sheets limit it.
Adjacent-industry substrate reuse like display glass; per-cm2 saving is closer to 2x than 10x and NiP limits to 300 C.
Fink-style fiber draw sliced into dies is a fresh combination; sub-um capillary breakup and face wiring alignment are doubts.
Rolled-up nanomembrane capacitors are established (IFW Dresden); footprint too large for DRAM cells.
Folding beats lithography only for capacity tiers; 2 GB/cm3 and 1 um TFT speed are far below DRAM.
Combustion processing of oxide dielectrics is published (Northwestern); 5 nm leakage unproven.
Silicatein biomineralization is known; protein residue, ions and low film density are poor for DRAM dielectrics.
Abnormal-grain-growth Cu(111) foils exist for graphene; lacks a matched low-leakage channel film.
Zero channel generation is appealing, but field emission is unidirectional and low-current; cannot write both polarities easily.
Metglas as barrier-free substrate is plausible; wheel-side roughness and 400 C limit; substrate is not the cost driver.
Ice templating gives micron pores; ~100 nm aligned control for cells is far off.
Magnesiothermic diatom-to-Si is known (Sandhage); random placement suits supercaps, not DRAM cells.
ALILE poly-Si is mature PV art; Al doping ~1e18 hurts access-device leakage.
Executable policy unlocking coating capacity, but TFT performance restricts it to capacity tiers.
Track-etched templates are known; 30-100 pores per node implies large cells, so density is limited.
